prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a layered layout: the camera wearer looks downward at near hands/tools and a bucket roughly 0.2–0.8 m away, ground and loose bricks about 0.7–2 m away, and upright reinforcement cages or gates roughly 1–3 m away, with their upper portions partly outside the frame. Bright hands in frames 3–5 are within the wearer’s arm’s reach and in front of the darker ground; the frame-5 arm enters from the right and extends leftward/upward toward the metal grid, while no separate full person is clearly visible. Across the sequence the viewpoint turns right: the bucket moves from central-left to right and then out of view, while the nearest grid shifts across the foreground and the right-entering arm becomes prominent. Depth makes near-versus-far separation and partial occlusion of the ground by the bucket, hands, tools, and grids clearer than RGB, but absolute metre estimates are uncertain and thin bars, shadows, frame edges, and the arm/tool boundaries produce unreliable or saturated depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to isolate objects and people, but it labels a large left-side ground/bucket region in frame 1 as “pizza,” a small upper region as “cell phone,” and a lower region in frame 2 as “teddy bear,” none of which aligns reliably with the RGB scene. Its “person” masks in frames 3–5 mostly correspond to partial arms or hands near the camera: a small upper-right fragment in frame 3, a lower-right fragment in frame 4, and a large arm entering from the right in frame 5, all roughly 0.2–1 m from the wearer and partly cut off by image boundaries. These masks help show that the close body fragments lie in front of and occlude the ground or metal grid, and that the visible arm shifts toward the right edge as the camera turns, but they do not establish additional full people, facing direction, gaze, or inter-person distance. Most scene structure—including bucket, bricks, soil, tools, and reinforcement grids—is left unsegmented, while the false class labels and fragmented masks make the map unreliable for object identity, count, and precise extent.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains only one yellow body-like skeleton in frame 4, positioned right of centre and apparently about 1–2 m ahead, with no magenta hand skeletons and no detections in the other four frames. If taken literally, it depicts a roughly upright figure with a small upper body above longer lower segments and a slight rightward orientation, but the corresponding RGB frame shows only close partial hands/arms and metalwork rather than a clearly visible full person, so facing direction, gaze toward the wearer, and limb reach cannot be trusted. The isolated detection could help indicate an articulated shape and its approximate left/right and above/below arrangement when RGB limbs overlap the background, yet here it appears spatially inconsistent with the visible evidence and may be a false pose assembled from tools, arms, or grid lines. Because it appears for one frame and vanishes immediately, it provides no reliable evidence of approach, retreat, turning, occlusion, or distance between people.
